diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Shahir Shahid Thalath said the transfer of US Patriot systems and refueling aircraft to Israel is more precautionary and defensive than preparation for an attack on the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that the US is trying to keep its military equipment out of reach of the Islamic Republic due to the possibility of escalating conflict.
The European Union stated at the IAEA Board of Governors meeting that the agency cannot confirm that the declared nuclear materials of the Islamic Republic have not been diverted from peaceful uses.

Esmail Kowsari, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that unity and cohesion must be maintained so that the US leaves West Asia and the region establishes its independence and integrity. He added that the enemy tries to open the Strait of Hormuz and attack Iran's nuclear program, but Iran has managed the country for over forty years despite sanctions and blockades.

Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said he considers the possibility of war high but that Arab countries in the region are deeply worried about suffering damage and the spread of war. He stated that if war occurs, US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and the UAE will also be targeted because these countries host US bases. Bakhshayesh Ardestani added that Iranian society is somewhat prepared for building nuclear weapons.

Behrouz Mohibinejadmabadi, the representative of Sabzevar in the parliament, said that the air defense capability of the Islamic Republic has increased in recent months and "F-35 fighter jets will no longer have a safe space in Iranian skies." He added that the Islamic Republic does not accept the condition of "neither war nor peace" and may take actions to break the blockade. He also warned that the Islamic Republic targets "offending" ships and tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and will target any area from which it is attacked.

Ali Belali, advisor to the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, said the armed forces of the Islamic Republic are fully prepared and ready to respond to any enemy miscalculation, and if any hostile action occurs, the enemy will face missile strikes. He added there are no limitations on the number of missiles or capabilities, and enemies have faced many difficulties countering Iran's missiles. Belali also said that if ordered, there is no limitation on using missile capabilities in new geographic areas.

Hossein Alizadeh, an international affairs analyst, said Trump is postponing the timing of the attack to next year to assess whether economic and attritional pressure against the Islamic Republic will be effective or if military action will be necessary.

A video sent to Iran International shows a citizen beside a road in northern Iran writing the slogans "From Savadkuh to Abdanan, my life is for Iran" and "Forever and a day, long live the Shah" on a wall.

In a volatile game, San Antonio Spurs defeated Los Angeles Clippers 124-112 with Victor Wembanyama's brilliance and returned to the top of the Western Conference with 13 wins and 3 losses. Portland Trail Blazers defeated Milwaukee Bucks 124-114 with a three-point storm by Tommie Kamara and recorded their tenth win of the season.

The Israeli ambassador to the United States stated that if Donald Trump decides to resume military attacks against the Islamic Republic, Israel will once again join the operations alongside the US. He said that planning for joint operations has been underway for months at the highest levels and considered the possible acquisition of chemical and biological weapons by the Islamic Republic a vital threat.

The cultural and artistic complex "Jaryan" in Qom was sealed by judicial order. Leili Golestan announced that the venue for the Jaryan book club event in Qom was sealed. The event was scheduled for Thursday, 28 Aban.

Farzin Karbasi, a journalist and political analyst, said there is a dispute between Kata'ib Hezbollah and the Iraqi government over control of the Jurf al-Sakhar area, and this agreement is fragile. He emphasized that armed groups supported by the Islamic Republic enjoy political, financial, and social support, and the Iraqi government faces serious obstacles in disarming them. According to Karbasi, there is a large gap between the Iraqi government's rhetoric about monopoly on weapons and its practical implementation.

Sky News reported, quoting Rob Magowan, commander of cyber and specialist operations of the British Army, that the UK is conducting offensive cyber operations against the Islamic Republic, Russia, China, and North Korea. Magowan described cyber threats against the UK as "significant" and said these countries must know that cyber operations against the UK will have a cost. He also said the UK is not at war but is in a cyber gray zone and that the UK's National Cyber Force has the capability to infiltrate enemy networks.
A video sent to Iran International shows a protester in Bandar Abbas burning the flag of the Islamic Republic and another citizen chanting "Long live the Shah."
A porter was killed following gunfire by military forces in the border areas of Baneh. This incident occurred today, Friday, 29 Aban.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, said on Friday, 29 Aban, that the Islamic Republic will make every effort for oil exports and negotiations amid reports of loading Iranian oil for export. He also said, "The blockade must be broken."

On Wednesday, 27 Aban, an oil tanker near the coast of Khasab, Oman was targeted by an unknown projectile, causing smoke to rise from the sea surface. The UK Maritime Trade Operations stated the tanker was targeted while exiting the Strait of Hormuz, six nautical miles north of Khasab. All crew members are safe, but the extent of damage and potential environmental pollution are still unknown.

According to information received by Iran International, Abuzar Bargahi, a royalist civil activist and one of the detainees of the December protests, was arrested to serve a five-year prison sentence and transferred to Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. A knowledgeable source said Bargahi was arrested on 7 Aban while giving flowers to citizens in front of his flower shop. This civil activist was initially sentenced to 9 years in prison, but the sentence was reduced to five years in the appeals court.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic has directed attacks on ships towards targeting specific and predictable routes in the Strait of Hormuz. He considered the increase in attacks on regional countries and threats to energy infrastructure in Europe and the US as signs of a more aggressive strategy by the Islamic Republic. Aghaei said the possibility of military conflict still exists and its timing and scale depend on Donald Trump's decision.

Citizens have reacted in messages to Iran International to statements by Masoud Pezeshkian, the president, about saving money and sleeping with a jacket. They have compared Pezeshkian's advice with the current economic situation and the high costs of clothing and marriage expenses.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said that a regional will has formed to end the activities of proxy groups of the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that the security and stability of Iraq and other countries in the region are tied to ending the influence of forces affiliated with the Islamic Republic and the monopoly of weapons in the hands of governments.

More than 90% of the workforce in Iran work under short-term temporary contracts or so-called "white signature" contracts; this situation has severely weakened workers' job security. Majid Rahmati stated that in the current law, labor unions and syndicates are not foreseen, and this issue, along with the expansion of temporary contracts, has limited workers' job security and the possibility of collective pursuit of labor rights.

Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United's new coach made news with drone footage of the practice. The drone operator stated that the flight was fully legal with all necessary permits and insurance. The footage shows training before Manchester United's match against Liverpool, but the main lineup is not confirmed.

A video sent to Iran International shows a fruit vendor protesting the tax set for his business. He points to the costs of house rent and car insurance and says, "How much profit does our load have that the government sets taxes of tens of millions of tomans for it?"

The Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh was hit by a missile attributed to the Houthis on Thursday, 28 Aban. The attack caused windows on seven to eight floors to break and damaged parts of the building's metal facade. The Saudi-led coalition said it neutralized the missile threat and initial assessments indicate debris fell and caused damage to the building.

The IAEA Board of Governors meeting focused on verifying the Islamic Republic's safeguards commitments and Tehran's adherence to UN Security Council resolutions ends today. Rafael Grossi, the agency's director general, reported that inspectors have access to Iran's nuclear facilities except for the Bushehr power plant.

Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said at the 'Pioneers of Liberation Congress' that revenge and retribution are our rights and the world will no longer be safe for murderers. He added that part of a great battle has been passed and part remains ahead. Vahidi also said the enemy ships do not dare to come within 500-600 kilometers due to the power of the naval and aerospace forces.

The Secretary-General of Kata'ib Hezbollah called on the members of the group to resume their normal activities and announced that disputes with the Iraqi Prime Minister will be resolved through special channels. According to the agreement, the group's forces will withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar within one month.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said the Islamic Republic is under increasing pressure to break the economic siege as its oil revenue resources near depletion. He suggested the government might try to engage in confrontation earlier to prevent worsening economic crisis and internal protests; however, he considers the start of a full-scale war dependent on decisions by the US and Israel.

A citizen criticized the increase in the price of the drug "Warfarin" in a video sent to Iran International. He said the price of each package of this drug rose from 100,000 tomans in early 1404 to 285,000 tomans in late the same year and is now sold for more than half a million tomans.

Mohammad Javad Haj Ali Akbari, the temporary Friday prayer leader of Tehran, announced that the armed forces have an order for unlimited and borderless action at a designated time. He said that if hostile actions are repeated, the armed forces will be ready to confront any scenario. He also added that the presence of US warships and military forces in the region is a sign of their pressure and erosion.

Bloomberg reported, quoting a senior Israeli Air Force official, that extensive missile attacks by the Islamic Republic during the war revealed weaknesses in Israel's air defense systems but also provided extensive information used to upgrade these systems. The official said the Israeli army was able to upgrade its defense systems within a few days. The 'David's Sling' system was also improved to counter a wider range of ballistic threats and now can handle continuous attacks lasting several weeks.

Leaders of Britain, Germany, and France emphasized European coordination in potential negotiations with Russia and the unrealistic nature of Moscow's conditions at the Berlin meeting. Meanwhile, the US special envoy announced Washington's efforts to reach an agreement with European support and said Russia has not opposed providing security guarantees similar to NATO's Article 5 to Ukraine.

Kazem Nourmofidi, the representative of the Supreme Leader in Golestan province, asked people to help manage energy consumption and ensure stable gas supply by reducing heating device temperatures by three degrees. He said if Tehran, Alborz, and Semnan provinces save gas consumption, better gas supply for northern provinces will be possible. Nourmofidi added that in the short remaining time, full compensation of this reduction through increased production is not possible and consumption management must be used.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, described the statements of the UK's senior military commander about offensive cyber operations against the Islamic Republic as indicating a shift in London's approach from reacting to threats to preventive and retaliatory actions. According to him, the Islamic Republic, Russia, China, and North Korea are attempting to weaken the security and deterrence of the UK and Europe using cyber attacks and hybrid warfare tools, and London is preparing to increase the cost of these actions.

The Instagram page Stadium 19 released a video showing the latest status of Azadi Stadium, indicating that the hybrid grass planting phase has been completed but the stadium tunnels are still under renovation. It was previously planned for the stadium to be ready for the 1406–1405 season, but the complete removal of the previous grass and planting of new grass has prolonged the preparation process.

In the ongoing review of the Iranian National Revolution in Dey 1404, information indicates that the head of the judiciary in Qom province was active in suppressing and confiscating the property of protesters. Farzad Fattahi discusses the protests and suppression in Qom province in the program "Geography of the National Revolution."

Dozens of trucks have stopped in a long queue at the Ramshar fuel station in Zabol county to receive diesel, and drivers say they have waited up to three days for refueling. Station officials have stated that the delay is due to a shortage of diesel. This situation has caused dissatisfaction among drivers and disruption in their work activities.

Yahya Saree, spokesperson for the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic, threatened on Friday, 29 Aban, in response to a warning from the Saudi-led coalition to evacuate the port of Al Hudaydah in western Yemen, that if this port is bombed, Saudi ports on the Red Sea coast will be targeted. Saree said that if the enemy carries out its threats to bomb Al Hudaydah port, the port of Jeddah and all Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast will be targeted by their forces.

Ahmad Alamolhoda, the representative of the Supreme Leader in Khorasan Razavi, said that people have two main concerns: the spread of unveiled women and livelihood issues. He added that people believe their innocent daughters are at risk and are also worried about the livelihood situation.

The public and revolutionary prosecutor of Oshnavieh announced the arrest of six suspects in the case of sexual assault on a woman with a disability in this county. Indictments have been issued for these individuals and their case has been sent to court for trial.

Amin Hayyan, the office manager of Yahya Saree, the spokesperson for the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic, announced that the Al-Shuqaiq power plant in Saudi Arabia will be targeted by the Houthis "within the next few hours." According to Saree, this attack will be "in response to the coalition led by Saudi Arabia's attacks on the Saada and Al-Mokha power plants in Yemen."

Two British men appeared today at the Old Bailey court in London in connection with the Fairford airbase incident. Prosecutors have accused one of them of cooperating with the intelligence service of a foreign country and the other of unauthorized entry into a restricted area with the intent to act against the security of Britain. Police consider this incident an operation in line with the interests of the Islamic Republic's intelligence service.

The National newspaper reported, citing Iraqi, Lebanese, and US security officials, that Islamic Republic agents have been traveling in the Middle East for over two decades using fake or others' passports and IDs, aiding Tehran's allied armed groups. The newspaper wrote that the Revolutionary Guards have expanded their influence over Hezbollah's decision-making in Lebanon during the past three years. Islamic Republic agents also remain present in various parts of Lebanon, especially the south, to support Hezbollah.

Mohammad Ali Abtahi, a reformist political activist, said that the Mossad intelligence agency is behind the hardline currents and efforts to remove Masoud Pezeshkian. Abtahi added that this organization, which can identify the sleeping locations of commanders, can also fuel a hardline atmosphere in Iran's political space.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing items purchased with a two million toman credit from the July ration card for two people and criticized the reduction in purchasing power and government policies. He said the Islamic Republic intends to remove or reduce this amount for some income groups.

Homayoun Falakshahi, an oil and energy expert, told Iran International that the US naval blockade has put unprecedented pressure on the Islamic Republic's oil exports. He added that it is unlikely China will risk serious confrontation with Washington to buy Iranian oil.

The death sentences of Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran, two defendants in the Ekbatan Town case and detainees of the nationwide 1401 protests, were confirmed by the Supreme Court. The death sentences of Mehdi Imani and Seyed Mohammad Mehdi Hosseini were overturned, and their cases were referred to a peer branch for reconsideration. These individuals were sentenced to death in early Khordad by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of moharebeh.

Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi, accused of leading the plot to attack the British RAF Fairford base, repeatedly disrupted the court session in New York and declared, "We are Qasem Soleimani's army." He denied charges related to terrorist actions. US prosecutors say Al-Saadi used coded language in phone calls from prison with his family to coordinate the October 5 attack on the Fairford airbase.

Real Madrid announced an official agreement with their Belgian goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois to extend his contract until June 30, 2028. Real Madrid ended speculation about Courtois's future with this decision and secured the experienced goalkeeper's presence for two more years. Courtois has been with Real Madrid since 2018 and has played in 348 matches for the team.

The Israeli army bombed a site in eastern Lebanon previously used for manufacturing and storing Hezbollah missiles. This is the second Israeli attack on this area this week. The official Lebanese news agency reported five Israeli airstrikes on this area.

The mother of Alireza Sedian Ghafarkhi, who died in the protests of Dey 1404, was present at her son's grave on her birthday and said she wishes for the destruction of oppression and oppressors who shed the blood of their loved ones. Alireza Sedian Ghafarkhi, 22 years old, was killed by government agents in Farrokhshahr (Ghafarkh), Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari province on 18 Dey 1404 [Gregorian: 2026-01-08].

Images released by Iranian fishermen on Friday, 29 Aban show an Iranian oil tanker near the Strait of Hormuz, reportedly preparing to move and pass through a naval blockade. Military sources of the Islamic Republic have warned that if this tanker is targeted, areas from Yanbu on the Red Sea coast to Fujairah on the coast of the Sea of Oman will be set on fire.

The Iraqi government announced the establishment of a new command center in Jurf al-Sakhar amid reports of the withdrawal of Kata'ib Hezbollah. Security officials stated that government forces including an army brigade, federal police brigade, Popular Mobilization Forces brigades, and an energy police unit will be stationed at this command center. The energy police unit is responsible for protecting oil pipelines.
A video sent to Iran International shows one of the protesters in Shiraz writing the slogan "Long live the Shah" on the wall of a public street in the city.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said the arrest and trial of Hezbollah members indicate a change in the political and legal conditions in Lebanon. He added that Israel monitors Hezbollah's movements throughout Lebanon and does not allow the group to rebuild its military strength by transferring forces and equipment from the south to other areas.

The Swedish Migration Agency announced that it has lifted the temporary restriction on processing asylum applications from Iranians, and cases will now be reviewed individually and under normal procedures. The agency emphasized that if the risk of arrest or torture upon return to Iran is proven, asylum support will be provided to applicants.
A video received by Iran International shows the trail of a missile fired in the sky over Qeshm on Friday, 29 Aban.
A video published on social media shows a group of schoolgirls in a classroom singing the anthem "Long Live the Name of the Homeland" and chanting "Long Live the Shah."
The operator of an Instagram page was arrested in connection with the protests of Dey 1404 in Abadeh county.

Persepolis football team defeated Paykan 3-0 in the thirteenth week of the Premier League. The goals for Persepolis were scored by Tiwi Bifuma, Mohammad Mahdi Mohibi, and Ali Alipour. With this win, Persepolis reached 26 points and returned to the top of the table.

A citizen criticized the scarcity and high price of the drug "Asentra" in a video sent to Iran International. He said this medicine is essential for neurological and psychiatric diseases and its price has reached 30,000 tomans per pill. He also referred to the government's performance, saying those who make a fuss over a single hair of girls see what people are suffering.
It was reported that at 18:45 an explosion occurred in the area of Qeshm city. It was also reported that a missile hit the Qeshm air defense.

A video released on social media shows that Farhad Mahdoudi's child said at his father's birthday at his grave: "You are the most heroic father in the world, happy birthday." Farhad Mahdoudi, 30 years old, was killed by direct gunfire from officers on the evening of 18 Dey 1404 in Mohammadshahr, Alborz province.

Amirhadi Anvari from Iran International reports that on 26 Tir 1405, while a ceasefire was in place, the United States attacked four bridges in Hormozgan province. These attacks became known as the "attack on the Bandar Khamir bridges," and by destroying these bridges, the coastal connection of the southern strip of the country was effectively cut off. These bridges were located on the coast of the Strait of Hormuz, on three east-west routes of the Strait of Hormuz.

Simultaneously with the Shenzhen meeting, Canada and Japan are seeking to expand their trade and defense relations to reduce dependence on the US. Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada, considered the cooperation of middle powers essential to reduce economic risks.

An alarm sounded on Friday, 29 Aban, in the city of Rzeszów in southeastern Poland. This alert was issued following a large-scale Russian attack on Ukraine and a state of alert declared by Polish authorities. Polish officials stated that at least one Russian missile hit Polish territory and they are investigating three impact sites as well as the possibility of a drone crash and a second missile strike.

Abbas Vahedian Shahroudi, a writer and civil activist imprisoned in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, faces multiple health problems including heart and lung diseases, high blood pressure, and gum infection, and has been deprived of access to specialized medical care. This political prisoner is held in ward 6/1 of Vakilabad Prison and experiences difficult conditions due to lack of necessary medications and insufficient medical facilities. Prison authorities only prescribe unrelated medications and he has not received specialized medical treatment.

Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst, pointed to the increase in femicide cases in Iran and said that the legal structure and the inability of the Islamic Republic authorities to implement effective measures hinder the fight against this phenomenon. She emphasized that raising public awareness, social sensitivity, and reliance on people and social networks are among the most important ways to combat femicide.
A video received by Iran International shows a long line of heavy vehicles waiting to receive diesel quotas in Mohammadabad, Hamun County, in Sistan and Baluchestan Province.

Aida Panahandeh, director of the series "Red and Black," reported the suspension of the release of the sixth episode due to censorship and editing. She said that the subjective sensitivities of some members of Satra have caused the entire series to be fragmented, and this process may lead to the destruction of the whole work. Panahandeh also criticized the lack of clear framework in censorship and said various scenes, such as fights and pulling a corpse out of a well with full covering, have been deleted.

Reports indicate a long queue of thousands of Iranian trucks carrying raw materials at the Yelme border crossing between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. The Uzbek media "Podrobno" reported about 990 trucks stopped and cited increased cargo transfer from China to Central Asia as factors worsening the traffic. The Uzbekistan Customs Committee confirmed the traffic situation, stating the videos showing heavy traffic were from a few days ago and according to official Kazakhstan statistics, only 100 trucks were waiting in line by 9 AM on Friday.

A video published on social media shows that members of Omid Rezaei's family, who died in the November 2019 protests, held his birthday anniversary at his grave. One family member said: "In the end, your pure blood caught them."

Videos received by Iran International show that on Wednesday, 27 Aban, a birthday ceremony for the late Mohammad Amin Kholaseh-Shar was held at his grave with the presence of his mother. Mohammad Amin, 23 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Fardis, and his brother Arslan ended his life about a month later due to grief over losing his brother.

Karim Bagheri, Persepolis coach, said in a press conference after the match with Paykan that he is not upset by criticisms and that everyone can express their opinion about the team. He also emphasized that his presence in the team has been at the request of various coaches and that past friendships should not influence coaching.

Ehsan Zabihzadeh, the spokesperson for the electricity industry, said the SMS sent about power outages in Tehran is related to network repairs and the timing of power outages will be announced. He also mentioned the possibility of planned blackouts starting from the coming weeks. These statements came after media reports about an SMS from the Tehran Electricity Distribution Company regarding two-hour power outages in the capital.

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, has spoken about a major plan to build social housing in the capital. Questions have been raised about the fulfillment of his promises, including housing construction and combating air pollution. Political issues in the country and mandatory hijab are also concerns of the mayor of Tehran.

A cafe in Shahriar county was sealed by the Public Places Supervision Police due to what was called "promoting corruption and immorality and possession of alcoholic beverages," and its operator was arrested.

Ahmad Nafisi, the political, security, and social deputy of Hormozgan province, announced that the explosion sound and smoke observed in Qeshm were due to the operation to destroy unexploded ammunition remaining from US attacks. Hormozgan officials had not issued any statement about the ammunition destruction operation before reports of the explosion in Qeshm. Tasnim News Agency reported that a missile struck an area on the outskirts of Qeshm city.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the grave of Mohsen Mohammadi Kuchaksaraei, a protester killed in the Mahsa uprising, and said: "We will soon take revenge for each and every one of you." This protester was killed on 30 Shahrivar 1401 in Qaemshahr.

In the past week, the main environmental news included the arrest of illegal hunters and fishermen, discovery of smuggled wood, ongoing air pollution in Tehran, Isfahan, and Khuzestan, closure of illegal wells, warnings about land subsidence, and actions against polluting units. This report is based on media and institutional reports and covers 126 independent environmental news items. Air pollution reached very unhealthy levels in several cities, and illegal wells were closed during a nationwide water and electricity operation.
It was reported that a widespread list of assassinations occurred in the first 24 hours of the operation.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said in a press conference after returning from his Asian trip that in a trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, he discussed in detail preventing the Islamic Republic from obtaining nuclear weapons. He emphasized that Iran will never have nuclear weapons, and the leaders of the three countries agreed on reducing nuclear weapons risks and preventing nuclear war.
A citizen sent a video showing slogans against the Islamic Republic and in support of Prince Reza Pahlavi and the people of Abdanan written in one of the metro wagons.
An 18-year-old young man in Jolfa County, East Azerbaijan Province, was spared from execution due to the forgiveness of the victim's parents.

A video shows a group of people in Mormori, Abdanan County, coming to the streets on the evening of Friday, 29 Aban, chanting slogans such as "Long live the Shah" and "This is the last battle, Pahlavi will return."
A citizen sent a video to Iran International, saying about the rising prices in Iran: "One kilogram of tomatoes and one kilogram of onions cost 373,000 tomans. Damn the Islamic Republic."

A relative of Soogand Sayyadi's family, a 16-year-old teenager from Kermanshah, said her father went to the school on the day of her death, beat her, took her school records, and threw her out of the window. The Kermanshah prosecutor confirmed that judicial investigations against Soogand's father are underway with charges including assault and murder, but the suicide hypothesis is also being examined. This source linked the violence on the day of death to years of beatings and threats by the father.

The head of Tehran City Council's Transportation Commission stated that about 46.5% of Tehran's air pollution is caused by worn-out vehicles. Jafar Tashakkori Hashemi said that about 60 to 70% of Tehran's taxi fleet is also worn out.

Nemat Afshar, a resident of Qazvin, has been detained by security forces for 26 days and is currently held in legal limbo in Choubinder prison in Qazvin. According to Harana News Agency, he remains in detention and is kept in judicial uncertainty.
Slogan writing as part of Iranian protests continues in various parts of Iran. A video received by Iran International shows that the slogan "Long live the Shah" was written on a wall in Hashtgerd.
Fardad Farahzad spoke in the Audio 24 episode about the extensive transfer of U.S. military weapons to Israel.

Reza Kermanshahi, advisor to Persepolis CEO, said after the match against Peykan that Persepolis protested to the referees committee and requested not to assign Isfahani referees for their matches because they are in the championship race with Sepahan. He also said that Tartar is sensitive to the Isfahani referee and was angry after the game.

Mauricio Pochettino, the new Manchester United coach, said they have come with the idea of building everything from scratch based on their own ideas and philosophy, aiming to create their own path and identity at the club. He took over after Michael Carrick's dismissal and started his work with meetings with players and staff. Pochettino stated his priority is to support the players to perform their best and said it is natural for players' confidence to drop when they do not win, emphasizing the need to believe in them.
On 29 Aban, a viewer sent a video from Ahvaz road, saying that refinery smoke caused severe air pollution and a "feeling of suffocation" for some citizens.

Following the maritime blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, the Islamic Republic's efforts to use land trade routes with China have increased. A video showing a long line of cargo trucks at the Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan border has fueled speculation about fuel and energy transfer via this route. Babak Zanjani reported heavy traffic on the transit route of goods from China to Iran on the social network X.

Axios reported that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, envoys of Donald Trump, met with senior Qatari officials in Berlin on Thursday, 28 Aban, to discuss resuming nuclear talks between Washington and Tehran. Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and Ali Al Thawadi attended the meeting. Trump stated that Iran wants a deal but does not accept one that is acceptable to him.

Alireza Nourizadeh, director of the Iran and Arab Research Center, said the presence of Kata'ib Hezbollah in Iraq has been questioned. He added that the Popular Mobilization Units should be examined separately, and the units expected to be stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar are probably coordinated with the Iraqi government.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi said the dispute between the Islamic Republic and the International Atomic Energy Agency over inspections of nuclear facilities is political in nature. He added that there is disagreement within the regime about developing nuclear weapons and some propose leaving the NPT treaty. Namvar Haghighi said increased monitoring capabilities make covert acquisition of nuclear weapons more difficult.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing extensive tree cutting in the forests of Amol and said this cutting is just near the road, and more trees have been cut further away.

Alireza Firouzja, an Iranian-born French chess player, became the champion of the first experimental edition of the Total Chess Budapest tournament by drawing against Anish Giri in the decisive Armageddon game. The tournament was held from November 10 to 20, 2026, in Budapest with 24 top chess players participating. Firouzja has competed under the French flag since 2021 and participated in the Candidates Tournaments in 2022 and 2024.

Alireza Beiranvand, the number one goalkeeper of Iran's national football team, won the Asian Football Golden Ball in 2026. Marzieh Jafari, head coach of Iran's women's national football team, became the best coach in Asia for the second time. However, these two selections are accompanied by ambiguities.

Shahram Khaledi, a Middle East history and international relations researcher, said that the increase in attacks by the Islamic Republic on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, the escalation of conflicts in Bab al-Mandab, and the rebuilding of Tehran's missile capabilities have increased the risk of renewed military confrontation. He added that the continuation of negotiations and the postponement of military decisions have so far benefited the United States more. Khaledi also said that the Islamic Republic's economic capacity has sharply declined, and continuing this situation could increase the risk of escalating conflicts.

Axios reported, citing two informed sources, that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, envoys of Donald Trump, met with senior Qatari officials in Berlin on Thursday to discuss mediation efforts to resume negotiations between Tehran and Washington. The Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar were also present at this meeting. Meanwhile, Donald Trump reiterated that he will never allow the Islamic Republic to obtain nuclear weapons.

Persepolis football team defeated Paykan with three goals in the 13th week of the Premier League and had a different performance from previous matches. Mohammad Taghavi from Iran International believes Persepolis should maintain this style of play against all teams and avoid fluctuations.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, told Iran newspaper that if the US wants an agreement, it must revise its position and take confidence-building measures. He said there is a possibility of reaching a formula to resolve the issue of 400 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%, with clear red lines including that these materials will not leave the country.

Videos received by Iran International show protesters in some cities of Ilam province writing slogans such as "Rise Iran" and "Long live the Shah" on walls and school doors, and burning government banners.

Recent controversies at Esteghlal began with protests over poor training conditions and lack of sufficient facilities, leading to the resignation of the team's head coach; the resignation was not accepted and the head coach returned to training.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi has warned about the risk of execution for Pouya Fakhrabadi, a taekwondo champion. His death sentence was issued in a show trial based on fabricated charges, and he was deprived of having a lawyer and the right to defense. According to information, the second branch of the Yazd Revolutionary Court sentenced him to death and three other defendants to 20 years of exile imprisonment each.

The spokesperson of the Saudi-led coalition announced that three ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis were intercepted and destroyed en route to Riyadh. The recent wave of drone and missile attacks by the Houthis on the Saudi capital has been widely condemned internationally. On Thursday, 28 Aban, a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's tallest skyscraper caused material damage but no injuries were reported.

Abdollah Mohtadi, Secretary-General of the Komala Party of Iranian Kurdistan, called the death of Sogand Sayadi, a 16-year-old girl from Kermanshah, a "horrific death" and said it is a source of deep sorrow and anger for everyone. He described violence against women and children as a blatant violation of human dignity and emphasized that guaranteeing the fundamental rights of women and children must be a pillar of any democratic platform for transitioning from the Islamic Republic. Mohtadi also referred to Article 301 of the Islamic Penal Code, which grants legal leniency to fathers in the killing of their children, calling it a weakening of the taboo against filicide.

Scott Busent, the US Treasury Secretary, wrote on X that the Islamic Republic's offshore oil reserves have run out and the regime may never receive revenue from oil previously sold. He also wrote that the authoritarian regime of the Islamic Republic always prioritizes its own interests over those of its citizens, even when ordinary Iranians face shortages of bread and fuel.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, emphasized that he will not allow Iran to obtain nuclear weapons. He said Tehran wants an agreement but is not willing to accept one that is acceptable to Washington.

China emphasized the role of cultural heritage and mutual understanding among nations in strengthening regional cooperation through cultural programs on the sidelines of the APEC meeting. These programs were held to show the link between culture, cooperation, and shared progress.

Reports about the possibility of the Islamic Republic attacking the US capital with a "dirty bomb" have received widespread attention recently. Donald Trump says the US is aware of the Islamic Republic's movements and will not allow such an action. The Islamic Republic has called these reports baseless and fabricated, considering their publication an attempt to justify further military attacks on Iran.
